items.summary: The pink ball was introduced for day-night matches over a decade ago, and in June this year the International Cricket Council (ICC) approved a trial of pink balls in Tests expected to be affected by bad light—subject to prior agreement from both teams.

items.summary: Penguin poop is fertilizing snow algae blooms along the Antarctic Peninsula, feeding dense green algae patches along the coastline, a new study shows. items.title: What makes a product 'Cool'?
items.summary: A teenager in Shanghai will wait in line for hours to get a Labubu doll. Meanwhile, a shopper in Ohio might drive across town to buy a robotic vacuum. Although buyers might call these products "cool," research shows they do so for entirely different reasons.

items.summary: Giving zoo lions whole carcasses on a feast-and-fast schedule appears to bring out more natural behavior. items.title: When U.S. embassies stopped reporting air quality, pollution rose
items.summary: For more than a decade, U.S. embassies and consulates provided independent, publicly available air-quality readings in cities around the world.

items.title: Conservationists are discovering 'bright spots' around the globe. Here's why they matter
items.summary: Every few years, the elders of Muluk, a tiny coastal community in Papua New Guinea, close a stretch of their reef to fishing. They do this to give these underwater gardens room to breathe, grow and replenish.

items.title: Children in improved homes face lower hospitalization risk, analysis finds
items.summary: Children living in houses improved through the Healthy Homes Initiative were found to be 30% less likely to be hospitalized in the following five years, according to research led by the University of Otago, Wellington—Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka, Pōneke.

items.title: Quantum computing shortcut makes particle collisions easier to simulate
items.summary: Collisions between particles at high energies can sometimes produce new particles and shed light on interactions between the fundamental constituents of matter. Simulating these collisions and their underlying processes could yield valuable insights into how matter behaves at extremely small scales.

items.title: 'Real opportunity' to boost low-carbon European holidays
items.summary: U.K. vacationers and the tourism industry have a "real opportunity" to shift to low-carbon European vacations, researchers say.

items.title: Plants, people and progress for native prairie seeds
items.summary: Across much of the central United States, there are ongoing efforts to restore native prairie. Returning native plants to the landscape can improve soil health and water quality and provide habitat for important wildlife and pollinators.
